title: ADM validation execution (adm-validation-result/v1)
description: The record of ONE test execution ADM spawned, and the only source of VERIFIED test counts. Produced by a runner adapter (manager/nextplan/runner.py), never by parsing a command's stdout: the adapter spawns an argv list with shell=False and reads the counts from the structured report the runner itself wrote. Codex demonstrated why, by running `echo documentation; pytest & echo ===== 12 passed in 3.10s =====` through ADM's validation path and obtaining VERIFIED tests_run=12 and a completed task. Legacy shell-string records still carry an exit code but can never carry counts. Round 6: this object is only a REFERENCE to an execution. Counts are read from ADM's own ExecutionRegistry entry for execution_id -- the `tests` field below is not consulted by the consumer at all -- because Grok obtained VERIFIED tests_run=999 from a hand-written block naming exec-forged, with nothing spawned. An execution_id ADM never issued has no entry, and therefore no counts.

execution_id.description: Identity of this one spawned process. Counts are attributed to it and cannot be reattached to another run.

argv.description: The argument vector actually spawned. Never a shell string: a shell string is the shape in which a printed argument and an executed program are indistinguishable.

runner.description: The adapter that produced this record. The adapter checks argv actually invokes that program.

started.description: False (or absent) means the process never started, which proves nothing and is rejected as evidence.

tests.description: Counts read from the runner's own structured report. null is the honest value when no report was produced -- the run is recorded, the numbers are not invented, and the completion proof fails for want of evidence rather than passing by omission. Since Round 6 this is the adapter's own copy for the audit trail; the consumer reads the registry, so a fabricated number here is inert rather than disbelieved.

output_summary.description: Bounded stdout+stderr, for humans reading the audit trail. Deliberately NOT a source of counts.

artifact_sha256.description: Optional. The digest of the runner's structured report. Never the source -- the registry's own digest is -- but a copy that disagrees means the record describes a different artifact, and the disagreement is not resolved in the record's favour.
